idiom_name: React element/render tree + host renderer (react-dom/client, react-dom/server, react-native)
implementation_notes: Stage one is the React element tree: components return platform-neutral elements and know nothing about the target. react.dev states the framework is platform agnostic - the same app could render to the web DOM or to a mobile/desktop platform's primitives - so the render tree is exactly the logical page the pattern asks for. Stage two is the host renderer chosen at the entry point: createRoot from react-dom/client for the browser, renderToString or renderToPipeableStream from react-dom/server for server HTML, react-native's renderer for native views. Keep channel-specific work at that entry point - no DOM access, window checks or layout reads inside components - and the same page serves web, SSR and native without duplication. For a non-React channel (e-mail, plain text) render the same data through a separate template or serialiser rather than importing a DOM renderer.
pitfalls: Components that read the DOM or window break every non-browser renderer, so channel-specific code must live at the entry point, not inside the page.
Server and client renders of the same tree must agree or hydration mismatches appear; dates, randomness and locale formatting are the usual culprits.
React escapes interpolated text but not dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so a 'logical' page containing pre-escaped markup either double-escapes or bypasses escaping entirely.
